story.title: Anthropic Launches Record IPO, Valued at $1.5 Trillion on Nasdaq
story.summary: Anthropic has begun trading on the Nasdaq following a record initial public offering (IPO) that raised approximately $81.3 billion. This valuation positions the AI company at around $1.5 trillion, surpassing SpaceX's previous record of $75 billion. Despite concerns about market volatility and public sentiment towards AI, the company's shares surged upon debut.

event_overview.title: About AI Industry
event_overview.subject: AI Industry
event_overview.summary: The event is Anthropic, PBC's transition from a privately held artificial-intelligence developer to a publicly traded company through the sale and Nasdaq listing of its Class A common stock. The listing made its shares available for public trading under the symbol ANT, while the company retained a public-benefit corporate structure and an unusual multi-class governance system.

facts.label: Listing date and market
facts.value: Anthropic Class A common stock began public trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026, under the ticker ANT.

facts.label: Offering price
facts.value: Nasdaq's listing notice identified an IPO price of $83.00 per Class A share.

facts.label: Issuer and legal form
facts.value: The issuer is Anthropic, PBC, a Delaware public benefit corporation; the company says its purpose is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for humanity's long-term benefit.

facts.label: Company purpose
facts.value: Anthropic describes itself as developing frontier AI systems intended to be reliable, interpretable, and steerable, alongside research and safety techniques for their deployment.

facts.label: Governance
facts.value: The company's filing describes it as a Nasdaq 'controlled company' because its Long-Term Benefit Trust, through Class T common stock, generally can elect a majority of authorized directors; the company also uses multiple classes of stock.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the November 19, 2026 public-market debut, not Anthropic's full corporate history, its subsequent share-price performance, or broader developments across the AI industry.

explore_lenses.label: What does this IPO signal for AI stocks?
explore_lenses.title: A new public benchmark for frontier AI
explore_lenses.summary: Anthropic gives public-market investors a direct way to price a frontier AI developer, but the debut also illustrates how quickly sentiment can move between the IPO price, the opening trade and the later market price.

claims.text: Anthropic priced 980 million Class A shares at $83; the company said 956.4 million of those shares were sold by Anthropic itself, while 23.6 million were sold by existing holders whose proceeds do not go to the company.
The $1.5 trillion valuation cited at pricing was not a fixed trading value: Reuters reported that the opening trade briefly implied about a $2 trillion valuation.

Reuters reported that analysts expect Anthropic to become a proxy for the broader AI trade, meaning investors may treat its subsequent performance as evidence about appetite for AI spending and valuations beyond this company.

explore_lenses.label: How did Anthropic reach a record listing?
explore_lenses.title: Revenue growth alongside steep costs
explore_lenses.summary: The company reached public markets after exceptionally rapid commercial growth in Claude-related services, but its SEC filing shows that scaling models and infrastructure has remained very expensive.

claims.text: Anthropic reported $4.59 billion of revenue in 2025, up from $386 million in 2024, and $16.29 billion for the first half of 2026, versus $1.16 billion in the comparable 2025 period.
Its SEC filing says consumption-based revenue accounted for 79% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, indicating that usage-based enterprise demand was its principal revenue source.

Anthropic cautioned in its filing that recent growth may reflect early-stage adoption and rapid customer expansion that may not be sustainable, and that its revenue-growth rate is expected to decline over time.
The same filing reported a net loss of about $104.0 billion for the first nine months of 2026, underscoring that fast revenue growth had not yet produced profitability.

explore_lenses.label: Will the proceeds cover its compute ambitions?
explore_lenses.title: New equity against vast infrastructure needs
explore_lenses.summary: The IPO materially expands Anthropic's financing capacity, but its disclosed compute commitments and planned private placement show that its strategy still depends on large outside capital and infrastructure partners.

claims.text: Anthropic said the IPO was expected to close on November 20, 2026, subject to customary conditions, and that underwriters have a 30-day option to buy up to 147 million additional Class A shares.

The prospectus says AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners agreed to purchase an aggregate $26 billion of Class N shares in a concurrent private placement, contingent on completion of the IPO and other conditions.
Reuters reported that Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, with some capacity dependent on financing beyond Anthropic's control.
The company's filing says its future cash requirements depend on factors including revenue growth, compute and infrastructure investment, and additional financing arrangements.

story_report.summary: Anthropic’s initial public offering raised $81.3 billion and valued the AI company at about $1.5 trillion at pricing. Shares debuted at roughly $98, while Reuters reported the opening trade briefly implied a valuation near $2 trillion. The debut gives public-market investors a direct test of whether Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth and heavy infrastructure spending can support the valuation attached to the broader AI trade.

sections.heading: Anthropic IPO Share Structure
sections.body: Anthropic priced 980 million Class A shares at $83 each. Of those, 956.4 million shares were sold by the company, while existing holders sold 23.6 million shares and retain the proceeds from those sales. The company said the offering was expected to close Nov. 20, 2026, subject to customary conditions; underwriters also hold a 30-day option to buy up to 147 million additional Class A shares.

sections.heading: Anthropic Revenue Growth and Losses
sections.body: Anthropic reported revenue of $4.59 billion in 2025, up from $386 million in 2024, and $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with $1.16 billion in the same period a year earlier. Consumption-based revenue represented 79% of revenue during the first nine months of 2026, making usage-based enterprise demand its main revenue source. Its filing also reported a net loss of about $104 billion over those nine months.

sections.heading: Anthropic Infrastructure Funding Commitments
sections.body: The prospectus says AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners agreed to buy a combined $26 billion in Class N shares through a concurrent private placement, contingent on the IPO’s completion and other conditions. Reuters also reported that Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, with some capacity dependent on financing beyond the company’s control.

unresolved.text: Early trading does not establish whether Anthropic’s valuation, or AI-sector valuations more broadly, will hold as more investors can trade the stock.

Anthropic warned that early adoption and rapid customer expansion may not be sustainable, that revenue growth is expected to slow over time, and that future demand and pricing may not offset rising compute costs.
The ultimate infrastructure capacity required, its cost, and the availability of partner and capital-market funding remain unresolved.

related_stories.title: Anthropic Achieves $2 Trillion Market Value in Nasdaq Debut
related_stories.summary: Anthropic reached a market value of $2 trillion during its Nasdaq debut, making it the first publicly traded frontier AI company. Shares began trading at $111.5, which was 34% higher than the IPO price of $83, as investors rushed to buy into the company known for its Claude AI model.
